newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-VAN GAAL FACES FIRST FOREIGN TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VAN GAAL FACES FIRST FOREIGN TEST.

text.p: New Barcelona coach Louis van Gaal will arrive in Spain knowing that his survival relies on repeating the success he achieved at Ajax -- domestic titles and the European Cup.
That could be a daunting challenge in Van Gaal's first foreign assignment, apart from a brief spell as a player in Belgium.
Van Gaal, the architect of Ajax's greatest triumphs, announced in October he would be leaving the club when his contract expired at the end of last season.
"I've achieved everything I can with Ajax. I now want to spread my wings," he said.
Announcing his departure, he said he wanted the challenge of a large club in one of Europe's top leagues.
"My ambitions lie abroad. I would like to go to a club comparable to Ajax," he said.

Rumours of his arrival in Spain swirled around the Nou Camp throughout last season, but the only hint Van Gaal gave was to say, during a beach training session with Ajax in the spring, that his next club would also be near a beach.
Van Gaal, 45, joined Ajax in 1988 and took over as coach from Leo Beenhakker in September 1991. He led the club to the UEFA Cup in his first season.

Ajax also won three successive Dutch league titles under his stewardship. But the pinnacle of Van Gaal's achievements as coach came with victory in the European Cup final in 1995 and the subsequent World Club Cup.

Ajax again reached the final of the European Cup in 1996, losing on penalties to Juventus, but the loss of Dutch internationals such as Edgar Davids and Clarence Seedorf a year ago to higher paying Italian and Spanish clubs saw their star fade.
They had a wretched start last season and could only claw back to fourth by the end.
However, that represented only a small blemish on a so-far fantastic career. In 60 "international" games under Van Gaal, Ajax lost only nine times.
As a player, his record was more modest, with spells at Ajax, FC Antwerp, Telstar Beverwijk, Sparta Rotterdam and AZ Alkmaar.

Tall and uncompromising, Van Gaal earned a reputation for discipline on and off the field. He is also largely credited with developing and expanding the club's much-vaunted youth policy -- which over the years has spawned Johan Cruyff, Johan Neeskens, Marco van Basten, Frank Rijkaard and Dennis Bergkamp. All left for sunnier climes.

At Ajax, the exodus has continued. Patrick Kluivert and Winston Bogarde have both signed for AC Milan while Marc Overmars will be playing for Arsenal. Danish captain Michael Laudrup is Ajax's only big-name signing so far.
One consolation is the club's towering Arena stadium -- a legacy of the success Van Gaal brought to the club.
Ajax's problem is that their stadium built for kings now has only foot soldiers to stock it.

At Barcelona, Van Gaal will at least have the resources to buy top talent. Ronaldo may be gone, but Dutch defender Michael Reiziger and French striker Christian Dugarry are both deemed likely to move from AC Milan.
Van Gaal is also expected to bolster his presence by taking his assistant Gerard van der Lem and goalkeeping trainer Frans Hoek with from Ajax.
If he does come good at Barcelona, one challenge may still remain.
A clause already rumoured to be written into his new contract would allow him to leave freely should he be named coach of the Dutch national side.
